title: Quarterly roadmap playbook for cohort lanes and model retirement runway
creator: Aisha Banerjee
project: Hosted API + Model Catalog Q2 Runway
description: Purpose: Define a repeatable quarterly playbook that maps cohort-driven capacity lanes (production, surge, experiment) to model catalog commit windows and a 12‑week model retirement runway. Scope: hosted API endpoints, model catalog rotation policies, canary windows, staffing handoffs to SRE/Capacity, and communications for customers and Sales. This ticket codifies decision criteria, success metrics, rollout steps, and contingency lanes for the Q2 runway so that PM/Eng/Design have a single source of truth for scheduling, risk, and operational handoffs.
goals: Create a lane-based cadence (Base / Surge / Experiment) for model commits with clear capacity and SLA expectations
Define a 12-week model retirement runway with customer migration notifications and deprecation telemetry
Establish canary windows and rollback criteria per lane, integrated with Console rollouts and observability dashboards
Reduce cross-team ambiguity by issuing a single quarterly schedule and on-call/staffing playbook for rollouts
acceptance_criteria: Published playbook in Confluence (team read access) with calendarized release lanes for Q2
Canary runbook and rollback checklist linked to the Console runbook and verified with SRE in a tabletop exercise
Model retirement email templates and in-console deprecation banners prepared and approved by Legal/CS
Dashboard widgets and cost/latency SLOs (per-lane) created in the Console; baseline numbers recorded
out_of_scope: Private (VPC/on-prem) deployment rotation mechanics — handled by Private PM stream
Kernel-level runtime changes — handled via ENG runtime roadmap tickets
key_decisions: Adopt 3 lane taxonomy (Base / Surge / Experiment) — chosen for simplicity and capacity predictability
Model retirement grace period: 12 weeks from deprecation notice with automated routing to compatible variants when available
Canary duration: 48 hours for Base lane changes, 7 days for Experiment lane flips, coupled with automated traffic ramping
tradeoffs_and_risks: Longer retirement windows reduce customer churn risk but increase operational burden and storage costs
Aggressive canary ramps reduce exposure but may increase latency regressions during peak traffic
Bundling many model swaps into a single lane reduces release overhead but increases blast radius

metrics_and_slos: Per-lane p95 latency target: Base <= 220ms, Surge <= 400ms
Token cost delta target relative to baseline: <= +12% for model variant swaps
Model retirement migration rate: 70% active clients automatically migrated or acknowledged within 8 weeks
